Card history shows predominantly in-person transactions; flagged online transaction is anomalous.
New device profile shared across 3 cards belonging to 3 different customers, indicating coordinated activity.
Card C12265-K2 shares 5 distinct device profiles with 8 other cards across 8 different customers.
Precedent cases matched this exact pattern with near-identical exposure and were confirmed fraud.
Card-not-present fraud from a new device shared across multiple unrelated customers is a strong indicator of coordinated fraud.

case.summary: Transaction 3509359 on card C12265-K2 was flagged with risk score 0.52. Investigation revealed the transaction originated from a new device shared by multiple unrelated customers (C02923, C02354) and connected via 5 device profiles to 8 other customer cards. Historical behavior is in-person, making this online transaction anomalous. Similar closed cases confirm this pattern as fraud. Fraud probability assessed at 0.88 based on multiple independent signals, triggering §6 stop.

next_best_actions.what_changed: Added BLOCK_CARD, DECLINE_TRANSACTION, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, GENERATE_REPORT, and FILE_REPORT after investigation confirmed fraud (p=0.88) satisfying R1 initial verification requirement and §3a SAR criteria.

sar.reason: Fraud confirmed (p=0.88), activity connects to shared device and other customers' potential fraud, pattern is coordinated per §3a.
sar.narrative: Transaction 3509359 ($125.08) on card C12265-K2 was identified as fraudulent. The transaction originated from a new device shared across multiple unrelated customers (C12265, C02923, C02354). Card C12265-K2 is connected to 8 other cards via 5 shared device profiles, indicating a coordinated fraud ring. Historical analysis confirms the transaction is anomalous compared to established in-person spending patterns. Precedent cases CC-2979, CC-4317, and CC-0832 match this exact pattern and were confirmed fraud.

stop_reason: §6: stopped investigating when p >= 0.85 with multiple independent pieces of evidence (new device, multi-customer device sharing, historical anomaly, precedent cases).
